reason: The smoke alarm has been unmounted for about 6 weeks (event-001, event-010). The landlord said he would use his own electrician but never named one, and no work is confirmed (event-004, event-007). The tenant was hospitalised and is vulnerable, and asked us to stop contacting them (event-012, event-013, event-014). On 20 Sep an unverified visitor came to the door and the tenant feared a scam (event-015, event-016). The visitor's link to the alarm job is unknown. Several policy reasons to escalate apply: a vulnerable occupant, a possible complaint about our contact, a possible security issue, and no clear contractor we can use. A plain chase or WAIT would not address those, and contacting the tenant would breach their request. I have also staged a request to the landlord for the contractor's identity and whether he sent the 20 Sep visitor. A chase was blocked because the landlord replied at event-007. No danger has been reported by code, so this is P1 rather than P0: there is no working-alarm status and the occupant is vulnerable. No money or approval is involved. The tenant's current alarm cover is unknown. If the landlord identifies the fitter and a visit is booked with the tenant's agreement, this could return to routine handling.

actions.summary: Smoke alarm at 26 Tallowmere Close has been unmounted since 7 Aug (about 6 weeks). The tenant, Elise Rowan, is a recently hospitalised, vulnerable occupant who asked us on 11 Aug to leave them alone. On 20 Sep an unannounced, unverified visitor knocked, and the tenant feared a scam. The landlord has given no contractor details since 12 Aug. A person needs to decide how to handle contact and the safety and security concerns.
known: Tenant reported the alarm off the ceiling on 7 Aug (event-001); no photos supplied.
Landlord said he would use his own electrician (event-004). He said on 12 Aug the work would be done by the following weekend (event-007). He gave no name, scope or appointment.
A fitter attended around 31 Aug-2 Sep, removed the bracket and could not refit the alarm because the box had no bracket. The alarm remains unmounted (event-010).
Tenant was admitted to hospital on 5 Sep and discharged by 11 Sep. They said the alarm was still unfinished and that they would arrange it and report back (events 11-13).
Tenant asked us to leave them alone because repeated calls and emails were upsetting. A pause was recorded (event-013, event-014).

On 20 Sep an unannounced person said they were there to check something. The tenant did not admit them. Identity, organisation and authority are unverified, and it is unknown whether they relate to the alarm job (event-015, event-016).
The tenant had earlier raised the knock with another agency contact, who passed it to a building-management contact (event-016).
No completion evidence is on file. There is no assigned provider, no quote and no approval amount.

Chased the tenant by email and calls (events 8-11)
I have not messaged the tenant, in line with their request. I am staging a short request to the landlord for contractor details.
options: Recommended: Ask the landlord for the fitter's name and company and whether he sent anyone on 20 Sep. Share the answer with the tenant only through a single gentle message or a channel they accept.

Have the manager decide whether a one-off welfare and safety contact with the tenant is justified. It would cover temporary alarm cover and advice not to admit unverified visitors. Consider offering an agency-arranged, landlord-approved provider.

Log the unverified visitor as a possible security incident and pass it to the building-management contact. Review whether tenant contact breached their request and whether it needs the complaints route.
